description:
# Compliance ticket for opi-q5k.18

Source check: opi-q5k.18 (truncate-to-width.test.ts audit)

## Implementation

Add to apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/wrap_ansi.ex:

    WrapAnsi.truncate_to_width(text :: String.t(), width :: non_neg_integer(), ellipsis :: String.t(), pad :: boolean()) :: String.t()

Semantics (matching tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/src/utils.ts truncateToWidth):
- Returns `text` unchanged if `visible_width(text) <= width`.
- Otherwise truncates so that `visible_width(result) <= width`, appending `ellipsis` bracketed by `\e[0m` resets (i.e., `"\e[0m" <> ellipsis <> "\e[0m"`).
- If `visible_width(ellipsis) > width`, returns `""`; with width exactly equal to ellipsis width, returns just the bracketed ellipsis.
- Preserves ANSI SGR sequences in the kept prefix (does not slice mid-escape).
- Tolerates malformed ANSI prefixes without hanging (the upstream test uses `"abc\e not-ansi ..."`).
- When `pad == true`, right-pads with spaces so `visible_width(result) == width`.
- Without ellipsis and `pad == false`, still appends trailing `\e[0m` when truncation drops a trailing reset.
- Contiguous prefix rule: NEVER skip a wide grapheme that does not fit and resume with later narrower content. Stop at the last fitting grapheme.

Also verify / extend `WrapAnsi.visible_width`:
- Must count tabs as 1 (width) inline (per upstream test `visibleWidth("\\t\\x1b[31m界\\x1b[0m") == 5` — tab=1 + CJK=2 + the 2 spaces? No — recount: tab(1) + ANSI(0) + 界(2) + ANSI(0) = 3. But upstream asserts 5. Upstream treats tab as width 4 inline per semantics in utils.ts. Inspect upstream implementation before coding and mirror the exact width attribution for tabs.) Confirm against src/utils.ts.

## Tests to port to wrap_ansi_test.exs (or a dedicated truncate_test.exs)

1. Very large unicode input (100_000 repeats of "🙂界") truncated to width 40 with "…" → `visible_width(result) <= 40` and result ends with `"…\e[0m"`.
2. ANSI styling preserved + reset-bracketed ellipsis: `"\e[31m" <> String.duplicate("hello ", 1000) <> "\e[0m"` truncated to 20 → width ≤ 20, contains `"\e[31m"`, ends with `"\e[0m…\e[0m"`.
3. Malformed ANSI prefix doesn't hang: `"abc\e not-ansi " <> String.duplicate("🙂", 1000)` truncated to 20 → width ≤ 20 (and completes quickly).
4. Wide ellipsis clipping: `truncate_to_width("abcdef", 1, "🙂", false)` → `""`; `truncate_to_width("abcdef", 2, "🙂", false)` → `"\e[0m🙂\e[0m"`, width ≤ 2.
5. Fits-already: `truncate_to_width("a", 2, "🙂", false) == "a"`; `truncate_to_width("界", 2, "🙂", false) == "界"`.
6. Pad mode: `truncate_to_width("🙂界🙂界🙂界", 8, "…", true)` → `visible_width == 8`.
7. No-ellipsis trailing reset: `truncate_to_width("\e[31m" <> String.duplicate("hello", 100), 10, "", false)` → ends with `"\e[0m"`, width ≤ 10.
8. Contiguous prefix: `truncate_to_width("🙂\t界 \e_abc\x07", 7, "…", true) == "🙂\t\e[0m…\e[0m "`.
9. Extend visible_width test: `assert WrapAnsi.visible_width("\t\e[31m界\e[0m") == 5` (confirm expected value by checking upstream tab semantics before hardcoding 5).

## Optional cleanup

Refactor the four component-local truncate helpers (select_list.ex:68, text.ex:24, tool_execution.ex, footer.ex) to call the new shared helper, since they currently slice by bytes/graphemes without ANSI awareness and will corrupt rendered output for styled/wide content. Bounded optional — ship the helper + tests first.

## Re-comparison (required)

After implementation + tests land, re-read tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/truncate-to-width.test.ts and confirm every upstream `it(...)` block has an Elixir equivalent. Post a final comment here before closing.

## Deps
Blocks opi-q5k.1 (acceptance gate).
